test_title: SSC Stenographer 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In the lac operon model, what is the primary role of the allolactose molecule?

options.text: It functions as an inducer, binding to the repressor protein and inactivating it.
It acts as a corepressor, binding with the repressor protein.
It binds to the promoter to initiate transcription.
It directly codes for the enzymes involved in lactose metabolism.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It functions as an inducer, binding to the repressor protein and inactivating it.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Allolactose acts as an **inducer** in the lac operon, which is a genetic regulatory system in bacteria.
 
• It binds to the **repressor protein**, causing a conformational change that inactivates the repressor.
 
• When the repressor is inactivated, it can no longer bind to the operator region, allowing transcription of genes responsible for lactose metabolism.
 
• This process ensures that the enzymes needed for lactose metabolism are produced only when lactose is present in the environment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lac operon:** It is a cluster of genes in Escherichia coli that are involved in lactose metabolism. It includes structural genes like lacZ, lacY, and lacA.
 
• **Repressor protein (lacI):** A regulatory protein that binds to the operator region of the lac operon to block transcription when lactose is absent.
 
• **Operator region:** A segment of DNA in the lac operon where the repressor protein binds to prevent transcription.
 
• **Allolactose:** A derivative of lactose formed by the action of β-galactosidase. It serves as the signaling molecule (inducer) for the lac operon.
 
• **Inducible operon:** The lac operon is an example of an inducible operon, which is activated in the presence of an inducer molecule like allolactose.
